provision_review.why: HB 463 closes division (xiii), the $65,000 amount, at December 31, 2026. It adds division (xiv), which from January 1, 2027 sets $70,000.00 for division (iii) taxpayers. The pre-fix retirement_income_exclusion_amount table runs open-ended from 1989 with band 12 at 65000. The post-fix module ends that version on 2026-12-31 and adds a 2027 version at 70000.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The three 2026 standard-deduction versions ($15,000/$15,000/$30,000) ran open-ended past 2026 despite HB 463's $375.00/$750.00 contingent annual increases from January 1, 2027, and the retirement-income exclusion table was encoded timelessly from 1989 at $65,000, so it neither carried HB 463's new 2027 division (xiv) amount of $70,000 nor distinguished the $35,000 amount the statute sets for taxpayers qualifying under divisions (i) or (ii).
triage.triage_notes: Multi-defect module; I picked the retirement-exclusion window as the decisive path because it both closes the timeless 1989-onward version and adds the corrected 2027 table (band 12: 65000 -> 70000). The parallel and equally supported defect is the three standard-deduction rules gaining effective_to 2026-12-31 plus new deferred_outputs entries for the contingent 2027 increases (same pattern as index 0). A third, distinct defect corrected here is an unrepresented_clause: pre-fix the single indexed retirement_income_exclusion_amount applied to every eligible taxpayer, while O.C.G.A. 48-7-27(a)(5)(A)(xiii) (read via the pinned corpus) sets '$35,000.00 for each taxpayer meeting the eligibility requirement set forth in division (i) or (ii) ... or an amount of $65,000.00 for each taxpayer meeting the eligibility requirement set forth in division (iii)'; the fix adds retirement_income_exclusion_amount_for_age_62_to_64_or_disabled (35000) and the derived retirement_income_exclusion_amount_for_taxpayer branch. HB 463 text confirmed for the 2027 division (xiv) $35,000/$70,000 split and the $375.00/$750.00 deduction escalators. The commit body is empty, so the quote is from the PR body; it names both the contingent-2027 deductions and the retirement-exclusion amounts/eligibility branches. Also present in the diff but mechanical: source-string normalizations (e.g. 48-7-27(a) -> O.C.G.A. 48-7-27(a)(1)(B)) and added effective-period excerpts.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical or as mere new coverage and could not: the diff changes real version windows, not just proof atoms — three standard-deduction rules gain `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` on their previously open-ended 2026 versions, and `retirement_income_exclusion_amount` gains `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` on the 1989 version plus a new `effective_from: '2027-01-01'` version. The pinned corpus confirms the pre-fix encoding disagreed with the source for 2027+: HB 463 rewrites (a)(5)(A)(xiii) to end "on or before December 31, 2026" and adds "(xiv) For taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2027 ... $70,000.00 for each taxpayer meeting the eligibility requirement set forth in division (iii)", while the standard deduction "shall be increased by $375.00/$750.00 annually beginning on January 1, 2027" subject to the paragraph (1.1) delay tests — so an open-ended $15,000/$30,000/$65,000 asserted amounts the source does not support past 2026. The module already listed `us-ga/statute/session-laws/2026/hb463/document-1` in its corpus_citation_paths and already encoded HB 463's 2026 amounts, so this is a correction of claimed scope, not new coverage. I considered amount_mismatch (the 65000→70000 cell) but that value lands in a newly added window rather than correcting a value inside an existing one, and the three standard-deduction rules change no number at all — the unifying, pinned mechanism is the effective period.

triage.verifier_notes:
Source verification (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current, corpus commit c5af541326e0): codified 48-7-27(a)(5)(A)(xiii) in the pinned text stops at "For taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2012 ... $35,000.00 ... division (i) or (ii) ... or an amount of $65,000.00 ... division (iii)" with no end date, and HB 463 SECTION 2-3 supplies both the December 31, 2026 cutoff and division (xiv). Verbatim HB 463: "such deduction shall be increased by $375.00 annually beginning on January 1, 2027, until such deduction reaches $18,000.00, provided that such increases in such deduction shall be subject to delays as provided in paragraph (1.1)".

A SECOND, coexisting fidelity defect is in the same diff and a reviewer may want it split out as its own case: pre-fix, `retirement_income_exclusion_band` was purely year-based (band 12 = current period → 65000), so a 62-to-64-year-old or permanently disabled taxpayer received $65,000 where the codified statute grants $35,000 under divisions (i)/(ii). The fix adds `retirement_income_exclusion_amount_for_age_62_to_64_or_disabled` (35000) and the derived `retirement_income_exclusion_amount_for_taxpayer` branching on `taxpayer_is_65_years_of_age_or_older_during_any_part_of_taxable_year`. That strand is unrepresented_clause (or wrong_entity_or_scope), not wrong_period; I kept the period kind because it covers four of the rules touched and matches the pinned rule_path rules[retirement_income_exclusion_amount].versions[0].effective_to.

Also in the diff but non-decisive/provenance-only: `source: 48-7-27(a)` → `O.C.G.A. § 48-7-27(a)(1)(B)` and `48-7-27(a)(1)(C)` → `O.C.G.A. § 48-7-27(a)(1)(B)`. Note the joint-return rule is HB 463's division (i) and the single/HOH/separate rules its division (ii); both are now labeled just (a)(1)(B), which is slightly less precise than before for the joint rule, but citation-string-only and mechanical.

Commands run were read-only (git show, cat, sed, resolve_provision.py). Confidence held at 0.8 rather than higher only because the commit is a 4-module campaign wrap-up whose message is generic; the module-1 diff itself is unambiguous.
